svg.aria-label: DDIA 3 · DATA MODELS & QUERY LANGUAGES sketchnote
svg.title: DDIA 3 · DATA MODELS & QUERY LANGUAGES: sketchnote
svg.text: The shape of the data picks the model: trees → documents, references → relational, relationships → graphs, history → events.
Document: a profile is a self-contained tree. One read fetches
it all because the data has locality. This works when the data
is one-to-many and read as a whole.
App code now does the JOIN
Document databases have weak join support, so the join moves
into application code. As data gains references, the relational
in Postgres; MySQL used to copy
handles both old and new shapes
shapes per type, or external data
rewrites the whole doc on update,
Weak or none; done in application
There is always a schema, it's just implicit in the reading code. You still pay
for migrations, just later and in more places.
Query: people born in the US who live in Europe → follow WITHIN* edges, any depth
A recursive query ("WITHIN, any number of hops") is one line in
Cypher and painful in SQL (recursive CTE).
write side: the log is the truth
read side: views are derived, rebuildable by replay
Commands are validated, then become immutable events in a log.
Projections build read views; fix a view by replaying.
Timelines store post IDs, then hydrate them
Star schema: fact table + dimension tables
Hotel content, product catalog page, chat message
Huge write volume, simple key access
"I start from access patterns. The two hot queries are X and Y, and both are key lookups with one join, so Postgres with the right indexes covers it. I'd
only move to Cassandra if write volume passes about 50k/sec."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
